body:
While we are looking at IE11 support, I see that our "external link" icons are broken too...

![Screenshot 2020-06-28 at 10 00 08](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15655/85943183-4114cf00-b926-11ea-87dc-9f5734a7c018.png)

Hi,

@gkalpak @petebacondarwin I took a look on the original issue

Its because of this: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/f8096d499324cf0961f092944bbaedd05364eea1/aio/src/app/shared/copier.service.ts#L46

seems like creating dummy textarea and then using `.select()` is causing the browser to scroll to the bottom
I still didn't find any workaround to fix this in IE11

Any suggestions how its possible to fix?

thanks

@gkalpak ,
After I checked more, I found the issue is not from `.select()` but its from `.removeChild()`
https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/f8096d499324cf0961f092944bbaedd05364eea1/aio/src/app/shared/copier.service.ts#L52

If I remove the above line, it doesn't reproduce

Also I tried to reproduce the issue in minimal project and its not reproducible.

I managed to fix this in another way:

I added id to the `pre` element here:
https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/f8096d499324cf0961f092944bbaedd05364eea1/aio/src/app/custom-elements/code/code.component.ts#L38

And then instead of `.appendChild` and `.removeChild` to happen on `document.body`, Its now happening on the `pre` element that I got by `document.getElementById`

This caused in IE11 to scroll to the pre element ( the code div) instead of the bottom of the page, no effect on other browsers

This cause the same affect to the scroll that you wrote, but happens only in IE

What you think?

issue.body:
The clipboard module works by creating a `textarea` dynamically, focusing it and copying its content. In order to prevent it from affecting the page layout, we put it at `-999em` off-screen, but the problem is that some browsers will try to move it into the view on focus by scrolling up.

These changes use `position: fixed` and anchor the textarea to the top of the page so vertically it's within the viewport.

body:
Thx for looking into this, @saifabusaleh! I looked into it some more and (thanks to your drawing my attention to angular/components#20073 :tada:) I found out that the odd IE11 behavior is due to removing the temporary `<textarea>` element while is has the focus (which implicitly happens when calling `.select()` on it).

I have created #38244 with the fix (and some other minor improvements to `CopierService`). PTAL and let me know if it works for you too.
